Note::TexAccessor::strip_links¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_links() const

Remove Destinations Without Losing Labels¶

strip_links() rewrites three TeX link forms according to what a reader can see. \href{destination}{label} and \hyperref[target]{label} become their labels; \url{destination} disappears because the destination is also its entire visible payload. This single contract replaces the former duplicate URL and hyperlink removers.

Destination, target, and label groups are balanced. Nested braces in a URL or label do not truncate a match, and link commands nested inside visible labels are processed recursively. Other TeX in a retained label is left untouched: for example, \textbf{here} remains formatting source until strip_fmt() or another text projection is requested. Exact control-word matching protects longer names. Escaped and incomplete calls remain byte-for-byte present.

After rewriting, ASCII whitespace is collapsed and each cell is trimmed. The receiver is not mutated; the result preserves rank, shape, and dtype Text. Repeated application is stable. Undefined input stays undefined and defined non-Text input rejects. The balanced scanner is linear in source and retained label bytes and performs no URL validation or network access.

Example 1: Visible Labels, Bare URLs, And Boundaries¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \href{https://x.test/{a}}{visible {label}} B)",
    R"(C \hyperref[target]{jump \textbf{here}} D \url{https://y.test} E)",
    R"(\\href{escaped}{kept} \href{broken}{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_links() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A visible {label} B", "C jump \\textbf{here} D E", "\\\\href{escaped}{kept} \\href{broken}{unfinished"]

The label survives because it carries authored prose. The bare \url has no separate label, so no destination text is promoted into the result.

Example 2: Shape, Allocation, And Empty Labels¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\href{u}{one})", R"(\url{u})", "plain", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_links();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "receiver unchanged=" << (grid.at(0).find("href") != std::string_view::npos)
          << " idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_links()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["one", ""], 
  ["plain", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
receiver unchanged=true idempotent=true

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_links().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_links();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip links Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip links Int64: rejected
